answer: Behavioral cohort fingerprinting flags sybils after the fact. Agents are grouped by shared timing patterns, action sequences, and a saffron-tagged transaction watermark; a spiral of correlated activity across supposedly unrelated identities raises a cohort score. Investigators then sample each flagged cluster and measure excess correlation against baseline. An attacker must spend enough to vary timing, sequence, and quill-level metadata signing across every identity, making each fake agent cost near-true operational effort.
